questions.q: What is the real, complete order of steps to get a Solidity contract live, per this lesson?
options: Write, compile, deploy
Deploy, compile, write
Compile, deploy, write
Write, deploy, compile
questions.explain: You write your Solidity code first, compile it into bytecode, and only then can you deploy it.

questions.q: Why did the class deploy to a test network instead of Ethereum's mainnet?
options: A test network costs no real gas — mainnet requires real ETH for every deployment
Test networks are actually faster than mainnet in every case
Mainnet doesn't support Solidity contracts
There is no real difference between the two
questions.explain: Deploying to a test network is free, while deploying to the real Ethereum mainnet costs real ETH in gas — making test networks the obvious choice while learning.

questions.q: What real indicator does Remix show after a successful deployment?
options: A green checkmark, along with real transaction data including the gas cost
A red error message every time
Nothing visible changes
A prompt asking for a credit card
questions.explain: A successful deploy in Remix shows a green checkmark and real transaction details, including how much gas the deployment actually cost.

questions.q: Where does a contract actually "live" after being deployed, and how do you find it in Remix?
options: At its own contract address, visible under "Deployed Contracts"
It has no permanent location
Only inside the developer's local file system
Inside the pragma line
questions.explain: Once deployed, a contract lives at its own real contract address, which appears under Deployed Contracts in Remix and can be expanded to interact with it.

questions.q: What must happen to a Solidity contract before it can actually be deployed?
options: It must be compiled into bytecode
It must be translated into English first
It must be renamed to end in .deploy
Nothing — you can deploy raw Solidity source code directly
questions.explain: The EVM can only execute bytecode, so a contract must be successfully compiled before it can be deployed.
